data.name: Tomboys Need Love Too!
data.detailed_description:
When Kai hears that his next door neighbor, Chris, will be staying with him while her parents are overseas, he thinks nothing of it. They're best friends, after all, and have been since childhood. To him, she's just "one of the guys", and a sleepover is nothing new.

But what Kai doesn’t realize is that, tomboy or not, Chris is now an adult woman. Furthermore, she has a strong sex drive, and she's planning to use their cohabitation as an excuse to show him sides of her that Kai never knew existed.

Just as Chris's advances begin to take effect, however, an obstacle appears: Sophie, Kai's most recent crush. She's a beautiful girl who radiates kindness, and naturally attracts people of both sexes towards her. Her only downfall appears to be that, for every nice word spoken about her, an equal number of heinous rumors drag her name through the mud...

Will the advances of Sophie, the girl whom Kai has been pining over for months, manage to sway his heart? Or will Chris finally convince him that the perfect woman was by his side all along?

Features:
  • 5 different endings depending on your choices
  • 2 romanceable girls
  • Hi-res artwork in 1440p resolution

reviews.review:
Tomboys Need Love Too! is a compact adult visual novel that takes the familiar childhood-friends romance and builds its central conflict around the moment when friendship begins developing into something more complicated. Rather than constructing an enormous cast or an elaborate fictional world, it concentrates on a small group of characters and a straightforward romantic dilemma. Kai has known his next-door neighbor Chris since childhood and has become so comfortable with her tomboyish personality that he essentially considers her one of his male friends. When circumstances lead to Chris staying with him while her parents are away, Kai initially sees the arrangement as nothing unusual. Chris, however, recognizes an opportunity to make him reconsider the way he sees her.

This setup gives the relationship a believable foundation because Kai and Chris already possess years of familiarity. Their chemistry does not need to be created from nothing, and much of the appeal comes from watching an established friendship cross boundaries that Kai previously considered fixed. Chris is considerably more aware of the attraction between them and actively tries to reveal a side of herself that her longtime friend has overlooked. The resulting interactions mix romantic comedy, awkwardness, sexual tension, and moments of genuine affection. The premise is deliberately uncomplicated, but the childhood connection makes the romance feel more personal than a scenario involving two characters who have only recently met.

The situation becomes more interesting with Sophie, Kai's existing crush. She represents almost the opposite kind of romantic attraction. While Chris is familiar, comfortable, and already deeply integrated into Kai's life, Sophie is someone he has admired from a greater distance. She appears kind, attractive, and naturally charismatic, yet rumors surrounding her reputation introduce uncertainty. This creates the story's most effective conflict because Kai is essentially choosing between the person he thinks he wants and someone he may have failed to appreciate despite knowing her for years. Sophie therefore serves as more than a simple obstacle placed between two childhood friends.

Player decisions have meaningful importance within this otherwise straightforward structure. There are two romanceable women and five possible endings, allowing different choices to steer the story toward noticeably different conclusions. The branching structure gives the experience some replay value because seeing one outcome does not reveal everything the narrative has to offer. At the same time, the limited number of romantic options means expectations should remain reasonable. This is a focused visual novel rather than a massive dating simulation filled with numerous character routes and complicated management systems.

Presentation is another important part of the package. The 1440p character artwork gives the visual side of the novel a cleaner appearance, and the anime-inspired designs fit the playful tone of its romantic and mature material. Since interaction revolves primarily around reading and making choices, the artwork carries much of the responsibility for establishing personality and atmosphere. The game also includes Steam achievements, trading cards, cloud functionality, and full controller support. These additions do not fundamentally transform the experience, but they make the overall package feel more complete.

The adult content is an important consideration rather than a minor optional element. Nudity and depictions of sexual activity are part of the experience, and Chris's sexual confidence is closely connected to the central premise. Consequently, this is better understood as an explicitly mature romantic visual novel rather than an innocent romantic comedy with occasional suggestive humor. Players interested only in wholesome romance may find its approach too direct, while those comfortable with adult visual novels will find the mature material more consistent with the story's intended tone.

Its greatest weakness is its relatively narrow scope. With only two major romantic possibilities, the narrative does not provide the breadth found in larger visual novels, and players who are not particularly interested in either Chris or Sophie may have little motivation to explore every ending. The gameplay itself is also intentionally minimal, relying on reading and decision-making rather than puzzles, exploration, combat, or deeper simulation mechanics. This simplicity is not inherently negative, but it makes character investment essential. The experience works best for players who enjoy visual novels specifically for dialogue, relationship development, branching choices, and alternate conclusions.

Steam Deck support is particularly good for a visual novel suited to portable play. The game is Steam Deck Verified, with its functionality accessible through the default controller configuration, readable interface text, and graphics settings that perform properly on the handheld. It also runs successfully under SteamOS. An earlier Steam Deck-specific fix addressed freezing behavior associated with Ren'Py games, further strengthening its suitability for handheld sessions. The combination of controller support and a reading-focused structure makes the Deck one of the more convenient ways to experience it.

Zetsubou serves as both developer and publisher, and the finished product reflects the priorities of a smaller visual novel production: a concentrated cast, straightforward storytelling, attractive artwork, adult material, and choices leading to multiple conclusions. It does not attempt to disguise its niche or compete with enormous narrative adventures. Instead, it focuses on delivering a specific kind of friends-to-lovers fantasy complicated by a second romantic possibility.

Overall, the game succeeds as a modest but enjoyable adult romance for players attracted to its particular premise. Chris provides the stronger emotional foundation because her history with Kai gives their changing relationship context, while Sophie introduces enough uncertainty to prevent the story from becoming completely predictable. The multiple endings encourage experimentation, the artwork complements the intimate narrative, and excellent Steam Deck compatibility adds practical value for handheld players. Its limited scope and simple interaction prevent it from becoming an especially ambitious visual novel, but within its intended niche it delivers a focused and reasonably replayable experience. 

Rating: 8/10
